key_insight: Which larval trait matters most depends on the local flow regime: swimming speed dominates in fast flow, while body shape dominates where recirculating flow alters alignment and retention.
engineering_relevance: The study offers a physics-based framework for predicting and potentially managing biological transport, retention, and settlement in complex near-bed flows and engineered coastal habitats.
method: Varied larval swimming speed and body shape from circular to elongated
Tested oscillatory flow over ridged substrates to isolate flow-structure effects
evidence_signal: Simulations showed settlement success could vary by up to an order of magnitude across trait combinations, with different near-surface flow structures acting as trait filters for transport, retention, and substrate encounters.
watch_item: The conclusions are simulation-based and tied to oscillatory flow over ridged substrates, so transfer to more irregular real-world habitats may require experimental validation.
paper_title: Flow regime determines whether larval settlement hydrodynamics are governed by swimming speed or shape
